The mathematical structure implies a competitive selection process governed by a max operator over competing reaction potentials. Each sER_i represents a distinct behavioral tendency, and their simultaneous activation creates a conflict. The system resolves this via a dominance rule, where only the maximum sER_i can proceed. This introduces a non-linear element into the otherwise linear threshold model. Inhibitory interference arises from mutual suppression, suggesting a form of associative inhibition akin to extinction effects. The resulting formalism supports both probabilistic inference in GSI and deterministic state transitions in GSE. The failure mode occurs when sER is insufficiently large or when competing potentials are nearly equal, leading to indeterminate behavior.
